items.content_html:
Description

This PR corrects several technical claims on the ARIA document role page.

Motivation

  • The example placed a document inside a dialog and called the dialog a composite widget. dialog is a window role, and the spec says the document role only changes assistive technology behavior inside a widget or application. The example now uses application, which matches the spec's own example, and a short note explains why a dialog doesn't need the role.
  • aria-expanded is not a supported state on the document role, so I removed it from the attribute list and from "Required JavaScript features".
  • tabindex is an HTML attribute, so I removed it from the ARIA attribute list. The keyboard interactions section now links to it instead.
  • Best practices now mentions that tabindex="0" adds the element to the tab order, and that widgets using arrow-key focus management need to let users reach the document content and get back to the widget.
  • The comparison with article said document elements have no relation to each other. The spec doesn't say this, and the issue points out it could mislead authors, so I removed the paragraph.

Additional details

  • Spec: document role (supported states do not include aria-expanded) and window roles.
  • markdownlint-cli2 and prettier --check on the page report 0 issues, and the front-matter linter passes.
  • Previewed with npm start: the page renders with no flaws, and the new roving tabindex anchor resolves.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #33746
items.title: Fix technical claims on the ARIA document role page

items.content_html:
Part of #40230.

"JSON object" is not a thing, and "JSON representation" is simply wrong: it returns a "JSON-serializable object".

I am using the exact same wording as JS pages, such as https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Temporal/PlainDate/toJSON, to explain how it's implicitly called:

The toJSON() method is automatically called by {{jsxref("JSON.stringify()")}} when an InteractionContentfulPaint object is stringified. This method is generally intended to, by default, usefully serialize InteractionContentfulPaint objects during JSON serialization.

items.content_html:
Fixes #23740

Specifically I've tried to address

  • Timing-Allow-Origin is needed for CORS and no-cors, it's for cross-origin protection
  • In the case of cross-origin iframes, responseEnd might measure when the iframe finished loading completely with all its subresources, not just the main resource.
  • encoded/decoded body size are CORS-protected rather than TAO protected

The pages weren't to our templates, so some sections moved into a description.

@noamr Is this something you could review? I think I understood this, but I did use Claude a bit for confirmations and it can be deceptive.
items.title: CORS / Timing-Allow-Origin resource timing

items.title: Add "read-only" to property pages whose interfaces already use them (1)

items.content_html: I don't know how dogmatic we are in enforcing that readonly properties are marked as readonly, but it's certainly a bug if a page is already using them and there exist readonly properties that aren't indicated as such, because then readers would assume that their absence means they are not readonly.
items.title: Add missing ReadOnlyInline to pages that already use them

items.content_html:
It might be okay for read-only properties to not be marked as such (our guidelines are murky) but it's never okay for non-readonly properties to be marked as such.

Namely:

  • Dictionaries are never readonly (MediaTrackSupportedConstraints)
  • Derived class members are protocols and can never be enforced as readonly (AudioWorkletProcessor.parameterDescriptors)

...others are just typos. They have never been read-only.
